tag: Episode 34 · The Sky of Twelve Houses
title: The Sky of Twelve Houses

beats.t: The ground beneath them rocked. Yeoni opened their eyes to a wooden deck. Beyond it, stars flowed like a river.
It was a ship. Instead of sails, great brass rings rotated in overlapping layers. Constellations were engraved on every ring.
What happened to the palace? We were just in a palace.
The palace folded itself into a ship. When the sky changes, so does the transport.
A ship? I can't handle ships. You think everyone from an island can?
Don't people from islands usually sail?
That's what makes it so unfair. Urgh.
Moka ran to the railing and tried to empty his stomach into the starry sea. Nothing came out, which only made him more miserable.
Neo sat at the bow, silver hair scattering in the wind. He had tucked his right hand inside his left sleeve.
Neo. Let me see your hand.
Both my feet are still attached. You mean my hand, right?
It went transparent earlier. I saw.
It's white now. If you want to see it, I'll show you later.
(Later. Always later. I'm writing that down.)
Yeoni opened their notebook. Seo Hanbi. Dragged away. Must find her. Above that, they added: Neo's hand. Must see it later.
A round table stood on the deck. Beneath glass, a circle shone in twelve sections. Brass rings around its edge stood still.
This sky's chart: a birth chart. When its rings stop, so does the ship.
Looks like a pizza.
Yes, a twelve-slice pizza. Each slice is called a house.
The ship creaked once and stopped. The star sea lapped its sides, but it moved no farther.
The chart's owner must press a house to turn the rings. The house holding the person you seek.
The house where Hanbi is? I don't know where that is.
Neither do I. Your sky, my lady. Only your hand works.
Yeoni first pressed the brightest threshold at the circle's far left. Stars gathered above it into a little pointed-eared cat.
A cat... Just like Yeongnyangi.
First house. Leo rising. Mr. Cat stands in your front entrance.
Neo adjusted his coat collar. He said nothing. Only the rims of his ears reddened.
Right beside it, Venus, the planet of love. Snug against the entrance.
You may skip that commentary.
Why? This is my favorite part.
That means stop pitching compatibility readings.
The rings didn't turn. Instead, the ship slid back a handspan. Somewhere beneath the glass, a chain wound one link tighter.
I'm seasick enough. Don't go backward too.
She pressed a silver point at the top, in the tenth house. The Taurus Moon.
The Moon. A place where your heart is visible to others.
That's a bit embarrassing.
True enough. Your cheeks turn red first when you're angry.
The ship slid back again. The chain sounded shorter and closer.
(Every wrong answer shortens it. Then the sound leads to the answer.)
She pressed her ear to the glass. The sound came from below the circle, just above the eastern threshold. Only there was the glass cloudy.
The room right behind the entrance. What's this one?
Twelfth house. The hidden room. The place of things confined.
Two red points wavered together behind cloudy glass. Mars and Jupiter.
The force to fight and the force to expand, hidden. Or someone hidden away.
(Someone hidden. Hanbi, you're there.)
Yeoni pressed both palms firmly against the cloudy square. It warmed beneath them.
The brass rings clunked into motion. The ship slid forward.
Got it. But the chain's two links shorter, right?
I know. So we have to hurry.
Before the meeting, Yeoni went to the bow. Neo leaned against the railing, gazing at the starry sea. Moka's groans drifted from a distance.
They say there's a big cat at the entrance. In my chart.
I heard.
I can tell you like that. Your ears are red.
The wind is cold. That's why I'm flushed.
The wind was blowing from the other side. Yeoni chose not to mention it and sat beside Neo.
Neo. When you first saw me, did you see my front entrance too? My first impression, I mean.
I did. You were angry, holding an umbrella that had blown inside out.
The worst.
You kept holding that inside-out umbrella until the end. That's the first image I remember.
Yeoni hugged their knees, brushing against Neo's shoulder. It was warm. Only his right hand stayed hidden inside his sleeve.
(Still won't show his hand. But that's enough for today.)
The ship suddenly listed. The brass rings screamed to a halt. One side of the sky was being erased.
A black circle passed between the constellations. Starlight vanished wherever it went, as though scooped out with a spoon.
The Black Moon. Astrology calls it Lilith. In this sky, that's Black Moon's name.
How many names does that thing have?
As many as the skies it has eaten.
Then it can't still be hungry. How many skies has it eaten?
Not eating from hunger. Empty, so nothing ever fills him.
(Never fills. A bottomless vessel. But they said that was me.)
Without realizing it, Yeoni pressed a hand against their stomach. It felt cold inside, as though something there was holding its breath.
The black circle stopped directly above the birth chart. The glass cracked. A star was plucked from the seventh house.
The seventh house. Partners. He's eating companions.
Neo reached for the railing and stumbled. His right hand had turned transparent again, this time above the wrist.
Neo!
Stand back. It's after me. Not you.
A voice seeped from the black circle. Low and gentle. Colder for its gentleness.
Well found, the twelfth house, vessel. Thy tiger is there.
Thou hast paid for knocking upon wrong doors. The chain shall keep shortening, link by link.
She's not my tiger. But I'm coming.
Yes. That is always how you come. Carrying an umbrella.
The black circle sank beneath the starry sea. Smoke rose from the empty place in the seventh house. Part of the sky remained missing.
The ship began moving again, slowly and on a tilt. The four gathered around the table.
Strategy meeting. The twelfth house opens only with its owner's birth time, down to the minute.
Eight thirty. Mom said it was just after her morning drama ended.
How do you know that?
I hear it every birthday. Including the drama's ending.
Good. Both you and Mr. Cat, who sits in your chart, may enter.
What about me?
Moka can follow. The door doesn't bar guests. However…
Yundal stopped. He laid his gloved right hand on the table. From the edge of the glove, a black crack crept toward his elbow.
I can't. I'm a passenger without an hour.
You can't cross the doorway because you don't have a birth hour?
Time is the key in this sky. Anyone without one slowly fades at the door.
Yundal's shadow faded across the table. Yeoni rubbed their eyes. It was still faint.
Then we find it. Your birth hour.
Blue Rabbit ran off with it. Who knows where in this enormous sky?
At that instant, a cheerful bell rang alongside the ship. Ding-dong. The bell of a shop door opening.
A cloud-shaped airship pulled up close beside them. Rabbit-ear sails fluttered. A sparkling advertisement hung along its side.
Dear customers! Blue Rabbit Finance has opened a branch in this sky too!
It's that rabbit. You haven't gone under yet?
Gone under? A new sky means a new interest rate! Today's special: starlight loans!
An hourglass hung around Blue Rabbit's neck. Its sand was pale pink, the color of the sky at dawn.
My Hour of the Rabbit.
Oh, our Hour of the Rabbit customer! You haven't been erased yet. How impressive!
Put that hourglass down.
No, thank you! This is the most expensive thing in this sky. You need an hour to open doors!
Blue Rabbit waved a forepaw. The airship slid away into the star clouds, its ear-shaped sails twitching tauntingly.
After her. Right now. We won't lose her.
My lady. Promise me one thing. When we catch that rabbit, you must be the one to find my hour.
Me?
I can't really remember when I was born anymore.
I still hate rainy dawns. At that hour, my hand goes cold first.
Yundal smiled as he spoke. The edges of his smiling face blurred little by little into the starlight. Yeoni studied it for a long time, determined not to forget.
Before Yundal had finished, Moka hauled on a rigging rope. The brass rings started turning again. The ship lunged forward.
Seasickness can wait. Those rabbit ears are going on a skewer today.
Moka, you said you couldn't handle ships!
I can't. That's why I'm ending this fast!
The starry sea struck the hull in silver spray. Ahead, rabbit-ear sails appeared and vanished between clouds.
My lady. Be ready to hear my story. To find my hour, we have to walk backward.
Backward?
It's called birth-time rectification. We trace the events of a life one by one and rewind to the moment of birth.
Yeoni opened their notebook again. At the top of a fresh page, they wrote: Yundal. Time of birth. Find it backward.
